findings.evidence: Lines 183, 191-192, 202-203, 310-311, 322-323, 348, 354, 361-362 carry `hk : 0 < k`/`0 < γ.energy`, `hp : -E < p`, `hpE : p ≤ E`, `hE0 : 0 < E`; none of the corresponding docstrings mention them.
findings.fix: Add the hypothesis to each of these docstrings, e.g. "...a target of energy `E` and momentum `-E < p ≤ E` against a photon of energy `k > 0`", or the equivalent "inside the forward light cone" phrasing already used for the collinear forms.
findings.issue: Docstrings of the real-photon and massless-target lemmas assert the relation with no condition, but the statements require `0 < k` and `-E < p ≤ E` (resp. `0 < k`, `0 < E`), and the relation is false without them: with E=1, p=-3, k=1 the system has T=2, P_∥=4, so exp(2y)=3 while (2k+E-p)/(E+p)=-3. Same pattern at lines 188, 199, 306, 318, 347, 353, 360. The sibling collinear docstrings (lines 116, 128, 140, 153) do state `|a - p| < k + E`, so this is an inconsistency within the file.

findings.evidence: Line 24-25 "The target has momentum `p` against the beam axis, so that `M² = E² - p²`"; `minkowskiProduct_add_self_of_target` (lines 94-96) takes only `hP`, `hP'`, `hM`, while `minkowskiProduct_add_self_of_realPhoton` (line 170) does say "unit beam axis".
findings.fix: Say "unit beam axis `n` (`‖n‖ = 1`)" in the module docstring lead, and note in the two `_of_target` docstrings that they hold for any `n` but that `p` and `q_∥` are the momentum and the component along the axis only when `‖n‖ = 1`.
findings.issue: The module docstring never says the beam axis `n` is a unit vector, yet almost every theorem assumes `hn : ‖n‖ = 1` and the stated convention `M² = E² - p²` only follows for `‖n‖ = 1`. `minkowskiProduct_add_self_of_target` (line 90) and `minkowskiProduct_add_self_of_target_energyFraction` (line 257) have no `hn`, so calling `p` "momentum against the beam axis" and `⟪q.spatialPart, n⟫` the component `q_∥` is only the intended reading for unit `n`.

findings.evidence: EpsilonEridani/QFT/Scattering/Photoproduction/Kinematics/Basic.lean:333-337 `theorem not_isReal_of_mem_photonRegion (hm : 0 < s.mass) ... : ¬ k.IsReal`, imported at InvariantMass.lean:8.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: the real-photon relations are the `Q² → 0` limit, and by `ChargedSource.not_isReal_of_mem_photonRegion` no photon in a massive source's `photonRegion` is exactly real, so the collinear (any-virtuality) forms are the ones that apply there.
findings.issue: "These real-photon forms apply exactly to the photons with `γ.IsReal`" tells a reader the real-photon branch is the applicable one, while the imported module proves that for a massive source that set is empty on the physical region (`ChargedSource.not_isReal_of_mem_photonRegion`). The PR description itself makes this point; the file does not.

summary: Module and theorem docstrings are otherwise accurate and name-checked, but the real-photon and massless-target docstrings state their relations unconditionally when the theorems are conditional (and the relations are false without the hypotheses), the unit-beam-axis convention is never stated in the InvariantMass module docstring, and the real-photon branch is presented as applicable without noting that the repo proves no massive source emits a real photon.
